How Much Will Your Tanzania Safari Cost?

Tanzania is not the cheapest safari country in Africa — and that is partly why parks feel less crowded and wildlife experiences stay premium. You can still safari well on a controlled budget if you book locally, travel in shoulder seasons, and choose lodges wisely.

A realistic planning range for a classic private northern circuit (excluding international flights) often falls between $2,000 and $8,000+ per person for 5–10 days, depending on comfort and season.

Budget Tanzania Safari Costs

From ~$350 pp/day private (or ~$250+ shared camping).

  • Simple lodges or tented camps outside park cores, or basic campsites
  • Private or shared 4x4 with pop-up roof
  • Park fees, guiding, most meals on safari days
  • Fewer “inside park” nights — more driving, still excellent wildlife

Budget does not have to mean poor guiding. Ask Our Team which current lodges deliver the best value for your month.

Mid-Range Tanzania Safari Costs

Roughly $450–$650+ pp/day — the sweet spot for most Tanzania Safari Magic guests.

  • Comfortable lodges and quality tented camps
  • Better locations (including more nights near wildlife)
  • Stronger guiding, flexible pacing, private vehicle
  • Ideal for Serengeti + Ngorongoro combinations

Browse mid-range options on our safari packages page and request a custom quote if you need different dates.

Luxury Tanzania Safari Costs

From ~$650 pp/day, with luxury+ often $1,500–$2,000+.

  • Prime camps and lodges inside or beside top parks
  • Larger rooms/suites, pools, refined dining
  • Optional light-aircraft transfers instead of long drives
  • Exceptional guiding and seamless logistics

Luxury pricing rises fastest when international agents resell local product — booking with Our Team in Arusha keeps more value in your experience.

Factors Affecting Your Tanzania Safari Cost

  1. Season — Peak dry (June–Oct) and calving (Jan–Feb) cost more; long rains can mean deals
  2. Lodge tier — Inside-park nights cost more than stays outside gates
  3. Group size — Private safaris for 2 cost more pp than 4–6 sharing one vehicle
  4. Transport — Fly-in segments raise comfort and price vs road circuits
  5. Park mix — Serengeti & Ngorongoro fees are higher than some southern parks
  6. Who you book with — Local operator vs overseas agent markup

Most first-timers choose the north. Explore all destinations or ask Our Team for a hybrid plan.

Other Costs: Fees, Tips & Cash

  • Park & crater fees — Included in most of our package quotes; rates change by authority year
  • Tips — Budget roughly $10–$20+ per person per day for guide/driver (group norms vary)
  • Visa & flights — Separate from safari day rates
  • Balloon safari — Optional add-on, often $500+ pp when available
  • Drinks & laundry — Check lodge inclusions

We list inclusions clearly on every quote so you are not surprised on the ground.

Tanzania Safari Cost FAQs

Is $350 per person per day realistic for a private safari?
Yes for a lean private budget safari with a local operator — simpler lodges, efficient routing, and fewer luxury extras. Mid-range comfort usually sits higher.
Why are Tanzania safaris more expensive than some other countries?
Park fees, logistics across large distances, and strong demand for Serengeti/Ngorongoro raise costs — while helping fund conservation and keeping visitor density lower in many areas.
Do your package prices include park fees?
Most Tanzania Safari Magic quotes include park fees, lodging, guiding, and safari meals as listed. Always confirm the inclusion list on your proposal.
How do I get an exact price?
Share dates and group size via our booking form or WhatsApp Our Team — we price live lodges for your window.

faqs.q: How much does a Tanzania safari cost in 2026?
faqs.a: Private budget safaris with a local Arusha operator often start around USD $350 per person per day; mid-range roughly $450–$650+; luxury from about $650–$2,000+ depending on lodges and flights.

faqs.q: What is included in typical safari prices?
faqs.a: Usually park fees, lodging, game drives with a guide/driver, and most safari meals. International flights, visas, tips, and some drinks are typically extra — confirm on your quote.

faqs.q: Is it cheaper to book a local operator?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Local operators avoid large overseas markups while providing the same parks and vehicles. Tanzania Safari Magic quotes directly from Arusha.
